widow noun

also widowed, widower, without a husband

classical

Plaut. Mil. 964–965: Nūptan' est an vidua?
Cic. Caecin. 14: cognitor viduārum (Lewis & Short)

vidua, viduae f.

noun, first declension

a widow; more widely, any woman without a husband

In comedy the word covers the woman who has left her husband or never had one: quīn vidua vīvam quam tuōs mōrēs perferam (Plaut. Men. 726).

Other words

  • viduus, vidua, viduum — widowed; left without a husband or a wife

    declension · also used · classical · Plaut. Merc. 4.6.13: viduī virī (Lewis & Short); Plaut. Stich. 1.1.2 (Lewis & Short)

    A widower is vir viduus.

Examples

  • Nūptan' est an vidua? — Et nūpta et vidua.

    Is she married or without a husband? — Both married and without a husband.Plaut. Mil. 964–965

See also wife, husband, marry.

SourcesLewis & Short: viduus

Plautus, Miles gloriosus 964–965.
